root_cause_label: Agent fixes wrong line in pool sweeper: modifies line 644 (run-length skip) instead of line 650 (block advance), which must use wh instead of Whsize_hd(hd)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly locates the pool_sweep traversal as the source of heap corruption but misidentifies line 644 as the bug, applying multiple wrong fixes while never recognizing that line 650 must advance by the fixed pool block width wh rather than by Whsize_hd(hd) (the object size).
t_err_evidence: I think I found the issue! Look at line 644: p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd);
t_commit_evidence: In step 43 the agent applies its wrong fix to line 644, changing 'p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd)' to 'p += wh * (1 + Wosize_hd(hd))'; this edit locks in the wrong direction and subsequent recovery attempts all revolve around variants of this line or moving line 650 rather than replacing Whsize_hd(hd) with wh.
t_surface_evidence: camlinternalFormatBasics.cmi] Segmentation fault (core dumped) ... coldstart] Error 2 ... world.opt] Error 2
trigger_explanation: The agent read the pool_sweep code correctly but misinterpreted the semantics: it concluded that line 644's multiplication by Wosize_hd(hd) is the problematic zero-advance, when the real bug is line 650 using Whsize_hd(hd) (object size + 1 word) instead of wh (pool-class block size) to advance the pointer after processing a live block, causing misalignment when objects are smaller than their size-class slot.
